answer: A stake-bonded reputation registry makes each agent's voyage through the economy costly to fake: to join, an agent locks a deposit and earns a verifiable history, like an opal that gains value only after long polishing. A new identity starts with zero trust and must accumulate attested work over time, so spinning up thousands of sock puppets in a nebula of fake accounts costs more in locked capital and waiting than any single fraudulent payout returns. Attackers face real economic loss, while honest agents keep their stake.
